dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: At (x,t), there exist vectors qt and qx that are respectively the derivatives of τ ↦ q(x,τ) at t and ξ ↦ q(ξ,t) at x, and qt + A qx = 0.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The vector PDE includes existence of both partial derivatives, not just a formal equation between derivative operators.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: There exist real eigenvalues indexed by the finite index type and a real basis of its real coordinate space such that each basis vector is an eigenvector with the corresponding eigenvalue.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The hypothesis is diagonalizability over the reals. It does not require distinct eigenvalues, symmetry, or an orthonormal basis.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005

binders: For every natural number m, including m = 0, let I = {0,...,m−1} and V = R^I.
For every real matrix A indexed by I × I satisfying the stated real eigenbasis hypothesis, there exist a function λ : I → R, corresponding to speeds, and a real basis b = (b_i)_{i∈I} of V.
The same λ and b are chosen before all subsequent universal quantifiers and work simultaneously for every q : R → R → V and all real x and t.
In the pointwise PDE equivalence, q, x, and t are arbitrary, and the scalar equations are quantified over every i ∈ I.

In the characteristic conclusion, q is universally quantified subject to joint differentiability and the vector PDE everywhere; the coordinate identity is universal in i, x, and t, and reconstruction is universal in x and t.
Within each local PDE predicate, the derivative witnesses qt and qx are existentially quantified and may depend on the function, coefficient or speed, and point; scalar witnesses also depend on i.
hypotheses: A has a real eigenbasis: there exist μ : I → R and a real basis e of V such that A e_i = μ_i e_i for every i ∈ I.
For the characteristic and reconstruction conclusions only, Q : R² → V, Q(x,t) = q(x,t), is real differentiable at every point.
For those same conclusions, q satisfies the vector PDE at every real (x,t): both partial derivatives exist and ∂t q(x,t) + A ∂x q(x,t) = 0.
conclusions: There exist λ : I → R and a real basis b of V satisfying all following properties together.
For every i ∈ I, b_i ≠ 0 and A b_i = λ_i b_i.

Write c_b(v)_i for the coefficient of b_i in v, and u_i(x,t) = c_b(q(x,t))_i. For every q and every real (x,t), existence of the two vector partial derivatives with ∂t q(x,t) + A ∂x q(x,t) = 0 is equivalent to the assertion that, for every i ∈ I, both partial derivatives of u_i exist there and ∂t u_i(x,t) + λ_i ∂x u_i(x,t) = 0.
For every jointly differentiable q satisfying the vector PDE everywhere, u_i(x,t) = u_i(x − λ_i t,0) for every i ∈ I and every real x,t.
For the same q, q(x,t) = Σ_{i∈I} c_b(q(x − λ_i t,0))_i b_i for every real x,t.
mathematical_definitions: V = R^I has coordinatewise addition and real scalar multiplication and its usual finite product topology.
Matrix action is (A v)_j = Σ_{k∈I} A_{jk} v_k.
A basis is a linearly independent spanning family; its coordinate map c_b is the real-linear bijection characterized by v = Σ_{i∈I} c_b(v)_i b_i.
The vector PDE at (x,t) means that there exist qt,qx ∈ V with d/dτ q(x,τ)|_{τ=t} = qt and d/dξ q(ξ,t)|_{ξ=x} = qx, and qt + A qx = 0.
The scalar transport PDE at speed λ_i means that there exist a,d ∈ R with d/dτ u_i(x,τ)|_{τ=t} = a and d/dξ u_i(ξ,t)|_{ξ=x} = d, and a + λ_i d = 0.
All slice derivatives are ordinary derivatives on the whole real line. Joint differentiability refers to differentiability of Q on R², not merely separate differentiability.
The constant 0 in q(x − λ_i t,0) is the initial time; the minus sign specifies translation by λ_i t from that initial profile.
translation.proposition_plain_english: Every finite real square matrix possessing a real eigenbasis admits a choice of real speeds λ_i and a basis b_i of nonzero eigenvectors such that the constant-coefficient system ∂t q + A ∂x q = 0 is pointwise equivalent, for every function q, to the scalar equations ∂t u_i + λ_i ∂x u_i = 0 for its coordinates u_i in that basis. Both sides of this equivalence include existence of the relevant partial derivatives. With this same choice of speeds and basis, every everywhere jointly differentiable solution on all of R² has each coordinate transported from time zero according to u_i(x,t) = u_i(x − λ_i t,0), and its vector value is the sum of these transported initial coordinates multiplied by their respective basis vectors.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The matrix is finite-dimensional, real, square, and constant in x and t. The claim is conditional on diagonalizability over R, not merely on real eigenvalues.
There is no positivity assumption on m. When m = 0, the index set is empty, V has only the zero vector, indexed assertions are vacuous, and reconstruction is the empty sum.
For matrices without a real eigenbasis, the implication supplies no conclusion.
Eigenvalues may repeat or be zero or negative. The basis need not be orthogonal or normalized, and its vectors need not have every standard coordinate nonzero.
The pointwise PDE equivalence has no independent continuity or joint differentiability assumption on q. Its two sides themselves assert existence of the relevant slice derivatives.

The characteristic formulas apply only to everywhere jointly differentiable solutions on the whole plane. Separate differentiability alone is not the stated hypothesis, and continuous differentiability is not required.
Space and time range over all real numbers, including negative time. No boundary, restricted spatial domain, or finite time interval is encoded.

The formulas use the existing solution's trace at time zero. There is no separately quantified prescribed initial datum and no explicit assertion that arbitrary initial data generate a differentiable solution.
The reconstruction determines any solution in the stated class from its time-zero trace, but the target does not separately quantify a uniqueness theorem comparing two solutions.
No weak, distributional, discontinuous-solution, stability, or continuous-dependence statement is encoded.
The speed family and basis are common to all functions and points; they are existential choices, not asserted to be canonical or unique.

For a q failing either global hypothesis of the characteristic implication, that implication gives no characteristic or reconstruction constraint. Constant functions do satisfy the hypotheses, so the solution class is not intrinsically empty.
